on_sale.label: Quality on sale
on_sale.rule: Profitable, revenue and earnings growing, not expensive vs peers — and trading at least 10% below its 5-year average price (or its average over all the price history on file, if shorter).

deep_value_intact.label: Deep discount, fundamentals intact
deep_value_intact.rule: Quality on sale, at least 20% below its long-run average, and cheap (value score 60+).

turning_up.label: Quality on sale, turning up
turning_up.rule: Quality on sale where the fall looks to have stopped: up over the last month and back at least 15% off its 52-week low.

steady_on_sale.label: Steady compounder on sale
steady_on_sale.rule: Quality on sale with a steady record: revenue and earnings up in at least 80% of the last six years, profitable every year, and low year-to-year volatility.

top_picks.method: Chosen by rule from the scores on this page, not by hand: fundamentally strong (for stocks, a multi-year record over up to six years: profitable in at least 80% of them, revenue and earnings up in at least 60% with positive growth rates and no boom-bust swings; growth at least median vs peers, counting how steady it was as much as how fast), plausible data, and not in the most expensive 20% — then ranked by opportunity score. Stocks also need a market cap of at least $2B, US-dollar financial statements, a US domicile (foreign listings' share counts don't yet account for ADR ratios), at least 3 years of reported history, and no open data-quality issue.
top_picks.evidence: Rule-based screens, not advice. Live track record so far: 14 overlapping weekly batches, average rank correlation -0.22 — not yet enough independent history to call it skill.

access_route.label: Investing from India
access_route.summary: Every market on this scoreboard is tracked via a US-listed ETF, so acting on any of these means buying a US-listed ticker. From India that runs through the RBI Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS): open a US-investing account with a platform that supports it, remit under LRS, then buy the ticker.
points: LRS caps outward remittance at USD 250,000 per financial year, per person.
TCS applies on LRS remittances above the current threshold — it is creditable against your income tax, not a sunk cost, but it affects timing of cash.

US-listed ETF gains are taxed in India as per your applicable capital-gains rules for foreign assets; foreign holdings must be reported in your ITR (Schedule FA). Rules change — confirm current treatment with a tax adviser.
US estate-tax exposure can apply to US-situs assets above certain thresholds for non-resident holders — worth understanding before large positions.
access_route.note: This names the route, not a provider. Any SEBI-registered platform offering US equity investing under LRS can execute it; comparing them is your call.

stock_coverage.why: Bottom-up stock rows come from SEC EDGAR filings, so only markets with US-listed (SEC-filing) constituents have them. Foreign-domiciled markets without US filers show none.
